reviews.author: ANNEZUE
reviews.text:
Everything was perfect and delicious.
I visited to celebrate my husband's birthday. I reserved a room and bought a cake from the hotel, but I was disappointed to hear that I could only light candles and not eat the cake. We added abalone and caviar with 45-year-old soy sauce, our signature menu, and Gapyeong Pine Tree, our signature dessert. They said that additional menus should be added equally according to the number of people in the party.

If you reserve a room, you will receive a glass of aperitif. My husband can't drink, so we drank non-alcoholic wine, and we were served a Korean herbal sparkling wine called Rapunzel, made at Yaksu Station. This one was seriously bitter, like goji berries.

The first course was a main course with Korean alcohol and small snacks. We were served 6 bites of food and a welcome drink of potato wine. It's a 13-degree herbal liquor made with steamed potatoes and glutinous rice, and the pairing with the food was really good. It felt like harmony was bursting out of my mouth.

It went great with alcohol and fries. They said that the inside of the fries was filled with snow crab meat and that perilla oil mayonnaise and cilantro were sprinkled on top. The soft texture was impressive.

The pork and potato tarak porridge came out refreshingly. They said they added domestic caviar in the center to make it more salty, but it was really salty. I liked the Tarakjuk because it had a smoky scent and a clean milk-like taste.

They said the crispy gamtae was filled with crab roe and sea grapes, but it was very salty and tasted like fried seaweed rolls.

The Korean chili sashimi and barley soybean paste were topped with cilantro and seaweed (gashiri). It was a taste that melted in my mouth.

The dumplings, which were made with top-quality shiitake mushrooms and white pepper mushrooms, were delicious. It was perfect with the firmness and rich taste of the abalone and the chewy texture of the dumpling skin.

They said the sauce on the bottom of the Korean beef jokpyeon was vinegared soy sauce, but the sauce was sour and very salty, like soy sauce vinegar. The jokpyeon tasted like beef bone, but it was like jelly.

The second dish was watermelon raw fish. He said the broth was refreshingly prepared using red pepper powder, watermelon juice, and grapefruit juice. It contained seasonal fruits and vegetables (mango, tomatoes, asparagus, celery) and cooked seafood (sea bream, rockfish, cuttlefish, scallops), and was topped with sweet shrimp sashimi. The texture of the cooked fish meat went well with raw raw fish. The soup was clean and had a watermelon flavor. The red pepper powder was spicy and the diced watermelon and celery had a nice flavor. It was the most unique raw fish dish I've ever had and it was delicious.

The third dish was steamed summer fish. You said you used a fish called Byeongeo. It came with pine nut sauce, and it was blended with herbs to create a sour yet savory sauce. It was completed with herb dill and fennel flowers on top. The fish meat was moist, soft and not dry. The sauce was sour, light, sweet, and had a pine nut flavor. The scent of the herb dill also went well with it.

The fourth dish was abalone and caviar with 45-year soy sauce. He said that he mixed abalone gently steamed in Cheongju with sesame oil and smoked domestic Osetra caviar to enhance the flavor. The caviar was fishy, ​​1.5 times larger than a 500 won coin, had a smoky flavor, and was salty overall.

The fifth dish was ‘Scent of the Sea’. He said that the gently steamed croaker was topped with sea squirt salted fish that had been salted and aged for 5 days, stir-fried razor clam, scallops, and a traditional Korean herb called banga. They said the broth they poured was clam broth, but it definitely tasted like sea squirt. The scent of the sea lingered and it matched the name of the menu. The croaker was soft but a little dry, so I wanted something crunchy like kimchi. The clam broth was light.

The sixth dish was truffle bean noodles. Finely ground truffle was placed on top of noodles made with morel mushrooms, green beans, and white-kang wheat. The bean noodles were the best. It was really flavorful and the noodles were soft. It had a fishy and pine-nut scent, and was the ultimate in savory flavor.The Schisandra Ade I drank in the middle was delicious. It was just right, not too sweet or sour, and I liked the refreshing sweet and sour taste of Schisandra chinensis. I highly recommend you try it.

Layered kimchi was served as the seventh dish. He said it was kimchi made by pickling cabbage, adding fillings, and then undergoing secondary ripening. The kimchi contained brisket, abalone, octopus, and shrimp. They said the cool soup was brisket broth, and the soup was incredibly refreshing. The abalone was chewy, the boiled pork tasted like beef on a fish belly tray, and the kimchi was crunchy. It was so refreshing and filling that I wanted to buy just the soup separately.

The main dish was served as the eighth dish, and the menu chosen was sweetfish pot rice and fish meat and soybean paste lamb ribs. He said the lamb ribs were marinated in soybean paste sauce for 24 hours and then grilled over charcoal. The sauce called fish meat soybean paste is a special soybean paste that is different from the existing soybean paste. It is said to have a richer flavor than the existing soybean paste because it is made with dried fish, meat, and other ingredients full of umami. Garnishes included cabbage, fried eggplant, and basil kimchi. Basil kimchi was unique. The scent of basil was noticeable, refreshing my mouth, and the lamb was delicious. It was the most delicious meal I've ever had. It was the softest, most moist and melted in your mouth. It was the best lamb of my life. The fried eggplant batter was soft and crispy like a cookie.

For pot rice, sweetfish was charcoal-grilled and mixed with rice. I heard that the rice was cooked using black mosi clam broth, and it tasted just like the rice. It was so delicious just eating the rice. There was mallow and dried shrimp in the soybean paste soup, but it was bland. Not a single seasoning was bitter. There were 5 side dishes, including young radish kimchi, sesame sprouts, dried chili peppers, deodeok, grilled red pepper paste, and royal-style braised beef. The overall taste was clean. You can eat it deliciously with pot rice and lamb ribs without having to add grilled strips.

Gapyeong Pine Tree, a dessert menu added as the ninth dish, was served. This is a dessert using pine nuts, a specialty of Gapyeong, the chef's hometown. Crispy pine nut meringue was served on top of pine nuts, topped with white ganache flavored with pine needles, and soy milk ice cream with vanilla beans next to it. It was like pine nut concentrate and the nutty flavor was no joke. As soon as I put the pine nut Baekseolgi in my mouth, I was immediately struck by the taste and aroma of pine nuts. Personally, I don't like rice cakes, but I was satisfied because the texture of Baekseolgi was something between bread and rice cake.

‘Ssalssalssal’ was served as the tenth dish. It is an ice cream made using three types of rice. The white ice cream below is made with white rice and a small amount of makgeolli, and the purple gelato above is made with black rice. The petal chips on top were said to be made with red yeast rice, and they were very crispy. It looked like a scorched rice cracker, and the ice cream made from black rice had a heavy taste.

The 11th dish included a 6-item refreshment kit. It came with red ginseng caramel, blueberry tart, traditional Korean sweets with ginger and prickly pear, madeleines with gamtae, juak made with glutinous rice flour and makgeolli, vanilla biscuits topped with mugwort and lavender cream, and a cup of warm tea.

The main music was delicious. The honey burst out inside and it was chewy.
The gamtae madeleine was attractive. It's unusual, but it's a taste that makes me want to eat it over and over again, and it's a taste that I keep thinking about.
The blueberry tart was nice because it was topped with deliciously ripe blueberries.

It was a very satisfying meal. I intend to visit again, and the server's service was excellent without any shortcomings. I ate well and left. Personally, I do not recommend adding caviar with soy sauce to the menu, and I recommend adding Gapyeong pine nuts.

reviews.author: YennaPPa (Luscious.K)
reviews.text:
#Cheongdam-dong #Seolya Galbi

“It’s still in its infancy... I can see a lot of room for improvement.”

A new rib restaurant has opened in Cheongdam-dong.
It is very different from other Korean barbecue restaurants I have experienced so far, with an impressive interior design, customer service, technology, and sincerity in food that are too impressive to be called a rib restaurant.
For that reason, it seems to be receiving rave reviews from gourmets and spreading word of mouth quickly.

Director Han Seung-seok, who led the success of Geumtan and Charcoal Jang, took two years to prepare this place, so it looks like he put a lot of care into it.

The interior is unique.
It feels like you are entering a dining restaurant rather than a meat restaurant.
The cool openness provided by the large windows on the first floor and the meat kitchen come into view, and after confirming the reservation, Usher guides us to the second floor.
There is a bar on the 1.5th floor to prepare drinks, and the dining hall on the 2nd floor is also cool with large windows.

The table is sturdy and wide, adding a sense of luxury, and the careful selection of flower pots, such as Singapore palm trees, which are popular these days, is also impressive.
The stone moss object is also pretty...

I also really like the way the servers dress.
Based on a Thom Browne-style gray cardigan, a modern mini apron added a professional feel and fashion sense.

All of the equipment was custom-made.
The water bottle, water glass, and highball glass all feature Seolya’s logo. Even the draft beer glasses were made by imitating the Usuhari glasses.
Overall, it was planned with a Korean feel and a high-end dining feel, making it a great setting for entertaining, serving foreign guests, and dating.

#appetizer
What's unique about this restaurant is that they serve appetizers like a real dining restaurant.
Since you don't receive any money, it's not the Japanese concept of otoshi, but a pure welcome dish.
This time, they gave me tarak porridge and cold chicken salad.
The salty tarak porridge is savory, the softness of the sous vide chicken breast, and the Chinese-flavored cold vegetable sauce with a hint of sanscho (Japanese pepper) flavor whet the appetite.

The appetizers don't end here.
The freshly fried spring rolls with a strong flavor are amazing, and the vinegared octopus salad is also delicious.
How can you not like it when it is given abundantly from the beginning?

#side dish
There are a total of 4 sides.
The cabbage salad added shiso (sauce) to the sesame sauce for added cheerfulness.
In fact, it was much better to eat than regular sesame sauce, and the texture was enhanced by frying the potatoes for a long time and turning them into crumbles.
The potato salad was excellent, surpassing most Ijikaya restaurants, and the neat japchae was also delicious.
They also gave us seasoned crab sauce, so we insisted that it was a Korean restaurant.
Namak kimchi has an artificially sweet taste and needs improvement.

#source
Three meat sauces are provided.
Regular salt, red pepper salt with red pepper powder and sesame oil added, and super soy sauce with ponzu, shallots, red pepper, and muoroshi added.
In addition, garlic oil used when grilling meat and lotus root, and coriander sauce used when grilling okra...
I really like the attitude of preparing various conditioners for the taste.

#Safe
It is called 26mm garlic tenderloin.
It's probably 26mm thick, which is the optimal thickness they found.
When grilling, a grilling technique is used to protect the meat juices and raise the temperature as much as possible by applying garlic oil to the meat.
And it is served after two restings for quite a long time.26mm is too thin for me.
I am dissatisfied with the thickness of this restaurant because I prefer Ttrak or Miu style tenderloin, which are my favorite tenderloin restaurants.
The grilling and resting are good, so the taste is good, but it is not extremely soft and feels quite dry and tough.

#raw ribs
I like it.
The meat quality and diamond cutting are also good.
The taste was doubled by proper grilling.
A rib restaurant wasn’t a rib restaurant for nothing.

#Chadol
Handmade cutting stone.
Of course it's delicious.
Instead, it's a bit tough.
You should grill it a little or make it a little thinner...

#meal
The meal menu is very disappointing.
It is said that soybean paste with a crab is famous, but it is neither red pepper paste stew nor soybean paste stew, but it has meat in an ambiguous position, crab and too many seasonings mixed together, making it a strange stew that is neither good nor bad. This is a menu that requires the aesthetics of subtraction, not the aesthetics of addition.

The bibim buckwheat noodles also leave a lot to be desired.
Special fruit sauce?
The taste is not deep and is just sweet.
There is no taste of ripening, so the outer taste is light.

It ruins a good impression at a meal.

#dessert
As a review event, if you write a review on Naver or Kette, you will receive a free signature shaved ice.
I chose the hojicha shaved ice and it was very delicious.
The scent of Hojicha is good (actually, it's closer to Earl Gray), but it's luxurious without being too sweet.
What the meal lacks, the dessert makes up for.

#good point
1. Comfortable and luxurious interior
2. Very friendly service
3. Server explains well
4. Free corkage for 1 bottle
5. Cheaper price than expected —> Byeokje Galbi Cheongdam Galbaen is overwhelmingly superior in cost-effectiveness and hipness.

#Improvements
1. Perhaps because it is still a soft off, it takes a very long time for food to come out. I guess it's because the kitchen can't fit.

2. The quality of the meals is still significantly inferior to that of competing meat restaurants. This can be easily seen by comparing it with Samwon Garden.

3. It's a minor detail, but the amount of rice is too small. If I go with my son, a strong young man, it would be two spoons, so how about giving him a little more?

4. The problem of meat preparation space is serious. The meat kitchen is open on the first floor, and has full windows, so the chefs at work can be clearly seen from the outside. It would be a perfect picture if the meat was neatly arranged and served, but it was broadcast live to see a lot of scrap meat piled up on the cutting board, toilet paper towels piled up on the cutting board, and not being properly organized, so I watched this with quite a bit of sadness while receiving the parking car. If it were me, I don't think I would want to eat meat at this place after seeing this.

5. No matter how modern Korean barbecue dining is, not having kimchi means throwing away the pride of Korean food. Of course, kimchi is a must.

6. There is a problem with the size of the resting bowl.
Do customers usually only order in 200g units?
It's just the right size to fit a 200g loaf.
We ordered 400g and requested to bake them all at once, but the roasting container was difficult to accommodate 400g. The lid does not close well, so press it tightly.
The juices from my tenderloin will drain out like laundry.

The food and service show differentiated attempts, preparation, and attention to detail, but it is still early days and there are many things that need to be improved.
I hope that you carefully select the areas of improvement and that the two-year plan will be a great success.

reviews.author: Taekyung Park (AniQ)
reviews.text:
0929:

A clean and tidy Korean grilled meat restaurant

Ganggangsullae Cheongdam branch, located in Cheongdam-dong, is a Korean grilled meat restaurant with an impressive clean atmosphere and attentive service. The quality of the meat is good, and the side dishes and vegetables are fresh, making it a very satisfying meal. In particular, the grill is well maintained, so you can enjoy grilling meat comfortably. The store is spacious and the spacing between tables is appropriate, making it suitable for family gatherings or company dinners. There is no delivery service, but the in-store experience is better.

reviews.author: Hanyang Monarch
reviews.text: Jangdokdae kimchi stew is different from other places and has a unique stew feel. The deep flavor of kimchi and the balance of the soup are well balanced, so you can feel the familiar yet addictive taste from the moment you take a spoonful. It is somewhat disappointing that with the store relocation, an additional charge of 1,000 won per piece for fried eggs, which was previously enjoyed freely, has been added. However, even considering such disappointments, the original taste of kimchi stew is still excellent, which is why I keep coming back for it. It's still a great option when you want a hearty meal without the burden.

reviews.author: Kunsup S
reviews.text:
After eating greasy food for lunch, I decided on spicy kimchi stew for dinner and searched for it. I found a kimchi stew specialty store closer than I thought, so I immediately went to Cheongdam branch of Jangdokdae kimchi stew.
It is located behind the Riviera Hotel at the southern end of Yeongdong Bridge, so it is easy to find. Seeing that the sign says “Driver’s Restaurant,” it seems to be a restaurant frequented by taxi drivers as well.

Even though it was past 8pm, the restaurant opened and there were quite a few customers. There were families eating not only kimchi stew but also grilled pork belly together.

Since it was our first visit, we ordered two servings of the signature kimchi stew and added just one more ramen.
Kakdugi, stir-fried odeng, seasoned bean sprouts, and pickled peppers were served as basic side dishes, but here, seasoned bean sprouts and chewy stir-fried odeng served as rice thieves.

After a while, the kimchi stew was brought out in a pot. After boiling it over a gas fire, the soup tasted somewhat bland for a stew. Although there were a few pieces of pork in it, it seemed difficult to create a rich soup, perhaps because the amount of meat was small. If I come back next time, I will definitely have to try the ham rice cake or meat sari.

Even though I ate it with ramen noodles, it felt like the stew was a bit insufficient for two people. Fortunately, there were unlimited rice refills, so I was able to fill my stomach with side dishes.

This restaurant has the decisive advantage of being open 24 hours a day, so I think it's a good option when you need a late-night snack or a late dinner.

reviews.author: My Diary Creatra
reviews.text:
I like seolleongtang. Moreover, my whole family loves seolleongtang, so it is one of our main dinner menu items.

Today, I came to the Fresh Seolleongtang Cheongdam branch to eat delicious seolleongtang. There's a place I used to frequent, but it's been a while since I've been there. The advantage of this place was that it had everything a restaurant should have: the flavor of rich soup, cleanliness, and friendliness.

Maybe it's been a while since I came here, but there are a lot of menus. So, I ordered the new menu item, pollack seolleongtang, and my family ordered regular seolleongtang. I ordered two children’s seolleongtang.

I had a very hearty dinner tonight. The dried pollack hangover soup I chose was also delicious. In particular, the children’s seolleongtang (seolleongtang) was excellent.
